  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

  Also Present:  Donald M. Davis, City Attorney

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386; LOCATION: 39 EMPTY SADDLE CLUB;
  APPLICANT: MICHAEL HASEGAWA (ON BEHALF OF VERIZON WIRELESS); A request
  for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-220387) for a new stealth telecommunication facility
  featuring a 64’-high monoeucalyptus structure located toward the rear of the property
  including 17 antennas (8 panel antennas, 4 CBRS antennas, 4 C-Band antennas, and 1
  microwave antenna) and 16 wireless radios on 4 arrays, a 342 square-foot lease area that
  features 3 equipment cabinets, 1 generator and will be fully enclosed with an 8’-high CMU
  wall.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. Included was
an overview of the applicable zoning requirements that must be met for the Commercial
Recreation (C-R) District. The proposed project meets all of the setback requirements. The
monoeucalyptus structure is proposed to be 64’t with the tallest antenna at 58’. The maximum
height for structures in the C-R zone is 44’ with an additional 20’ for telecommunication facilities
if the following findings can be met:

  •  There is no feasible alternate location.
  •  Exceptional circumstances that require the facility to exceed the required height limit.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that the applicant provided a letter and coverage area map for
justification that an additional wireless facility is needed in the area. The applicant considered the
South Coast Botanic Gardens and the former Palos Verdes Landfill, however engineers
determined that 39 Empty Saddle Road would be the best location to provide coverage for the
areas in need of better signal.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff has received letters in support and opposition of the
project; those in support cite increased coverage in the area especially with emergency services
and those in opposition raise health concern issues due to radio frequency radiation, property
values, aesthetics, and overall land use compatibility.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided an overview of the FCC order in relation to local
governments purview. Staff have also determined that the project has met the Conditional Use
Permit findings.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open
the Public Hearing; Take public testimony; Discuss the issues; Close the Public Hearing; and
Adopt Resolution No. PA-220386.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

Michael Hasegawa, Delta Group Engineering on behalf of Verizon Wireless, provided an overview
of the operation of the wireless facility and stated that maintenance and operation will be
unmanned and will not generate any traffic. Routine maintenance occurs every 4 to 6 weeks. Mr.
Hasegawa stated that Verizon has two project objectives for wireless facilities, which are provide
signal coverage of sufficient strength to achieve consistent, sustainable, and reliable service to
customers and/or to provide additional system capacity to offset the contraction of signal
experienced when nearby facilities become overloaded. Mr. Hasegawa stated that nearby sites
are overloaded, and that the development of this facility will improve the existing conditions for
customers in the area and provided additional information on the need to improve signal in the
area. Mr. Hasegawa stated that Verizon Wireless telecommunication facilities operate at the
lowest power level; well below the standards used by the FCC for safe human exposure to radio
frequency electric magnetic fields.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if the facility will be subleased to other emergency services
agencies. Mr. Hasegawa stated that if emergency services agencies or another carrier wanted to
co-locate, they will need to go through the same process. This wireless facility could
accommodate other wireless facilities; however, he confirmed that at this time, this is only a
Verizon Wireless facility.
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES,
OCTOBER 2, 2023
  2
 COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about any reported fires due to similar wireless facilities.
Mr. Hasegawa stated that the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) required that these
wireless facilities have a generator in case of an emergency and as far as he knows there have
been no fires caused by generators nor the wireless facility.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the material used for the “tree”. Mr. Hasegawa
stated that he does not have this information, but this could be provided.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked why this application was continued on two previous
Planning Commission agendas. Mr. Hasegawa stated that Verizon Wireless and Delta Group
wanted to be cognizant of the concerns of the residents and a community meeting was held on
September 11 where an expert on electromagnetic emissions provided testimony on safety
issues. Mr. Hasegawa stated that it took some time to coordinate this meeting.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked how many people were in attendance. Mr. Hasegawa
stated that city staff provided a copy of a petition, and those residents were contacted to attend
the meeting.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked Mr. Hasegawa if he felt that the concerns of the residents
were adequately addressed. Mr. Hasegawa stated that he did.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked Mr. Hasegawa for photos of other similar faux tree wireless
facilities. Mr. Hasegawa stated that he did not, but they could be provided.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if there are other similar wireless facilities on the Peninsula. Mr.
Hasegawa stated that there are dozens of carriers who have wireless facilities on the Peninsula.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked how many similar wireless facilities have been approved
in the city. Director Naughton stated that there are several building/façade mounted wireless
facilities throughout the city and many in the public right-of-way.

In response to a question by CHAIR YOO, Mr. Hasegawa provided an overview of the various
panels/antennas proposed for this project.

CHAIR YOO inquired about the levels of RF emissions. Mr. Hasegawa stated that he does not
have that information but stated that it is within FCC regulations.

 In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Mr. Hasegawa stated that this
particular location on the site was chosen since it met all of the applicable standards of the
municipal code and allows for the best signal to go out.

CHAIR YOO asked about the lease term. Mr. Hasegawa stated that this information is proprietary
and confidential.

Joe Peterson, on behalf of the Empty Saddle Club, provided a presentation addressing the
objections and concerns of residents, which include:

  •  Concern: Multiple Carriers.
  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that it is his understanding that the tower is for Verizon
  Wireless and one other carrier; the size and appearance does not change with additional
  antennas.

  •  Concern: Increased Generators/Fire Risk.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that generators will be tested for 10-15 minutes once a
  month and will only turn on during a power outage. They were not able to find an instance
  of fire starting due to wireless facility generators. If there was a fire concern, the project
  would be abandoned.

  •  Concern: Increased Commercial Traffic.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that traffic was surveyed over three days going in and out
  of the Empty Saddle Club. There were no less than 25 commercial vehicles each day. Mr.
  Peterson stated that per Verizon, there will be service vehicles at the site one to two times
  per month.

  •  Concern: Risk of cancer through its microwave system.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that the majority of radiation from these types of facilities
  are radio frequency (RF) waves and not microwave radiation.

  •  Concern: Height of the tower.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES,
OCTOBER 2, 2023
  3
   •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that there are nearby phone poles that are 60 feet and this
  is only an additional 4 feet.

  •  Concern: View of tower daily.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that he could not find one home with a director line of site
  to the tower. It’s possible that the tower may be seen from the second floor of a home.

  •  Concern: Property value.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that he looked at several sources for research and stated
  that per a study by Valbridge Property Advisors, the maximum movement in value up or
  down was 3%.

  •  Concern: Verizon approached the Empty Saddle Club.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that the Empty Saddle Club has been looking for a solution
  for several years. Their concern is for safety and cell service in this area. On the adjacent
  trail from the Empty Saddle Club to the little league baseball field, there is very limited cell
  service.

  •  Concern: An agreement between the City of RHE and the Empty Saddle Club regarding
  lease restrictions.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that the agreement is in regard to non-members leasing
  the club for events and activities.

  •  Concern: Legal action between the Club and the City.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that there is not and never has been any legal dispute
  between the Club and the City.

  •  Concern: The Club does not have a right to dictate to the homeowners to live with this
  item.
  •  Response: Mr. Peterson stated that this is not the Club’s desire. The Club has a right to
  have a fair and honest debate and the same access to emergency services as immediate
  surrounding areas.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if the Empty Saddle Club reached out to Verizon. Mr. Peterson
explained that they reached out to three consulting firms; Delta Groups is a subconsultant to
Verizon and they went from there.

CHAIR YOO asked for clarification regarding the microwave antennas proposed for this project.
Mr. Peterson stated that it is his understanding that there is minimal radiation from the microwave
antenna for this project. He added that it’s under the FCC maximum for repeated human
exposure.

In response to a question by CHAIR YOO, Director Naughton stated that the CUP runs with the
property and any enforcement would be the responsibility of the property owner to address.

In response to a question by CHAIR YOO, Mr. Peterson stated that it is not the intention of the
Empty Saddle Club to enter into a long-term lease agreement.

COMMISSIONER LOADSMAN stated that the plans show the trees at approximately half the
height of the proposed tower and inquired if the trees are trimmed due to the proximity of the
power lines. If there are concerns with the view lines from the easterly properties, allowing them
to grow may protect the view of the cell tower. Mr. Peterson stated that they would have no issue
with that as long as it does not infringe on the power lines.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if there are any numbers regarding the radiation from the
microwave antennas. Director Naughton stated that attached to the agenda there is a statement
letter of the proposed facilities’ compliance with FCC guidelines.

Mr. Hasegawa quoted the FCC Section 704 of the 1996 Telecom Act.

In response to a question by CHAIR YOO, Director Naughton stated that the Planning
Commission is not approving any level of RF associated with this project; what is being approved
is whether the facility is maintaining compliance with FCC guidelines.

Don Davis, City Attorney, stated that the Planning Commission is not approving specific RF’s;
they are required to comply with the FCC. The applicant stated in his presentation that these
facilities are typically below the FCC requirements. Once the facility is operational, there is a
requirement in the city’s code that they provide a report showing that they meet all FCC
requirements.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES,
OCTOBER 2, 2023
  4
 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that he would like to know at a minimum the percentage
of the current allowable limit.

Attorney Davis stated that he understands the concerns; as staff has noted and the applicant has
stated with the RF, this in an area of preemption. There is a condition of approval that a report be
provided within 60 days of operation showing that the FCC requirements are being met. Attorney
Davis is recommending that this be reduced to 30 days. This report will provide critical data since
it will be when the facility is operational. The extent of the city’s scope to regulate RF’s is to ensure
that the facility is in compliance with the FCC.

Janelle Hartley, Municipal Engagement Partner, Verizon Wireless, stated that carriers must
purchase licenses from the FCC, within the licenses that are purchased, they must abide by the
frequency ranges. She stated that she is happy to work with the engineers to forward the
frequency transmissions for each antenna, but they are well below the FCC limits. Ms. Hartley
stated that at the community meeting, an independent expert was brought in to speak in regard
to iodizing and non-iodizing radiation and its health effects. During the community meeting he
went in depth on the frequency and how well below they were on the range of emissions.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked how the FCC monitors each site. Ms. Hartley stated that
she will need to come back with that information.

CHAIR YOO asked if there are reports provided to the community. Ms. Hartley stated that there
are no reports provided to the community, however they are heavily regulated by the FCC and
CPUC that if any issue were to arise, the issue must be analyzed and reported to those agencies.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Attorney Davis stated that he
understands the concerns and there is no issue with questions regarding compliance however
beyond that it cannot be the overriding factor in the decision. The design will comply and there is
the requirement of the report. Attorney Davis stated that as Ms. Hartley pointed out that these
systems can only work within a certain frequency level once they are set up. In terms of Verizon
being the applicant, this is not unusual. If an issue were to arise, the permittee would likely be
contacted first, however, the property owner could also face liability for their tenants under the
city’s municipal code.

CHAIR YOO asked about the agreement between the city and the Empty Saddle Club that was
signed in 1994. Attorney Davis stated that he and Director Naughton reviewed the agreement as
well as the minutes; this agreement came about with the redevelopment of the clubhouse and
concerns from the residents regarding the activities of the clubhouse. When analyzing the minutes
and the examples it was determined that they were all related to events type of activities. Even if
the agreement had restricted this proposed use, the Club and Verizon could seek to amend the
Conditional Use Permit.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that according to the FCC website there are three
instances when they routinely look at facilities, which are at the original construction, after any
modification, and at renewal. In her experience in working with these types of facilities, the FCC
has standards that they apply, and Verizon also has obligations to make sure that they are in
compliance otherwise they run jeopardy of losing their license(s) and being penalized.

CHAIR YOO stated that he understands that their decision cannot be based on the RF number,
but he still would like to know what that number is. Mr. Hasegawa stated that procedurally,
Verizon, Delta Groups Engineering, and the Empty Saddle Club have provided pertinent
information. The CUP requirement was 60 days for that information and if the RF number had
been requested beforehand, they could have had that information for this meeting. However, the
information regarding the RF number for each panel can be provided at a later date.

Rob Hammond, 23 Middleridge Lane, Rolling Hills, stated that he is president of Los Caballeros
in Rolling Hills and former board member at Rolling Hills Little League. He stated that there has
been extensive discussion on the RF’s, which cannot factor into the Planning Commission’s
decision. Mr. Hammond stated that Rolling Hills is working on property values and safety. He
stated that he feels that their property values are hindered by the lack of cell coverage. The Empty
Saddle Club can provide cell coverage for Rolling Hills Estates in an area that is highly active. Mr.
Hammond shared a story about a woman who was thrown off her horse and broke her back. She
could not call out to get help and was only found after her horse returned to the Empty Saddle
Club without a rider and a search began. Mr. Hammond had to call the fire department and take
them to the woman’s location since there was no cell coverage. Mr. Hammond stated that this is
a fantastic location, and this area would be highly benefited by this cell tower.

Darren Eades, 14 Pinto Lane, stated that he has resided there for ten years. He had a co-coach
who had a heart attack going up the hill and if Mr. Eades wouldn’t have been able to get to the
top of the hill to call for help, he would have died. He also shared that a kid broke his arm and he
had to carry him to get him to his car to get him help because he could not call 911. In another

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES,
OCTOBER 2, 2023
  5
 incident he was accosted in his barn by a homeless person and could not call 911. Mr. Eades
stated that this is not about RF’s and rather about keeping the community safe.

Evan Williams, 7 Empty Saddle Road, stated that he and his wife have resided there since 1986.
Mr. Williams stated that he strongly opposes the application to construct a multi-story radiating
wireless facility in his neighborhood operated by Verizon and leased from the Empty Saddle Club.
Mr. Williams stated that the project does not and could not meet all of the property development
standards set forth in RHEMC Section 17.22.050 that are required to be constructed in the C-R
zone and are not mentioned in the staff report. If the city approved the CUP and Verizon
proceeded with the construction of the facility, then this would constitute a breach of an agreement
signed by the city, the club, and the homeowners. Mr. Williams stated that all of the roads in the
neighborhood are private roads and in part his opposition is due to the burden placed on the road
system which is not maintained by the City. Mr. Williams expressed his concerns with details not
included in the staff report and with regard to the number of opposition letters which were
received, which were seven times those received in support of this project. Mr. Williams stated
that RHEMC 17.22.050(H) was not included in the staff report and is the one that the
neighborhood cares most about. It states, “Vehicular Access. There shall be adequate vehicular
access from a dedicated improved street or service road.” Mr. Williams stated that this does not
exist in this neighborhood and this requirement cannot be met without the approval of the
homeowner’s association. Mr. Williams stated that he disagrees with the statement regarding
the agreement and stated that this was due to a dispute that related to the use of the Empty
Saddle Club property by the club and having multiple shows that had increased the traffic on
the road system among other factors. Mr. Williams stated that the property is also in a Landmark
Overlay Zone and quoted RHEMC Section 17.38.010. Mr. Williams also expressed his concern
with decrease in property values due to close proximity to cell towers. Mr. Williams provided
copies of his analysis to staff.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Mr. Williams stated that the
agreement is specific to any lease to a non-club member for any activity.

Keri Zickuhr, !8 Empty Saddle Lane, stated that she stated that Mr. Williams, Mr. Eades, and
her are the only ones to speak so far who live in Rolling Hills Estates. She would like to strongly
oppose the cell tower and communications center proposed by the Empty Saddle Club. She
stated that his was proposed by the Empty Saddle Club, they called Verizon, for among other
reasons, to lower their dues and to provide income for their sporting activities. The residents
and Rolling Hills Estates citizens did not call for the cell tower. Ms. Zickuhr stated that the city
does not have to approve this proposal due to this being a bad coverage area and suggested
that the cell tower be placed at another location which may make more sense. Ms. Zickuhr
asked if city engineers could look at other locations that could be better for the city. In regard to
the community meeting, she did not receive notification of how to join this meeting and stated
that they did not do a very good job in reaching residents. Ms. Zickuhr stated that this cell tower
does not fit in with the aesthetics of the city. It was mentioned that there was a wired capability
for a landline and asked why this could not be reinstalled. Ms. Zickuhr stated that a former
employee emailed her that it is the intent that this facility be used by other carriers. She asked
the city to use its discretion on aesthetic design and to review the agreement.

In response to a question by VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR, Ms. Zickuhr stated that her biggest
concern is the unknown and after it is constructed the FCC can do whatever they want. She
also expressed concerns with her child having anxiety over this cell tower being installed.

CHAIR YOO asked if the cell tower being 44’ would make a difference and if the cell tower
would be in her line of site. Ms. Zickuhr stated that the height would not change her stance and
she is not sure if she would be able to see it but stated that she can see the telephone poles.

Ellen Pagliano, 40 Empty Saddle Road, read a statement written by her daughter. The letter
was emailed to staff and copies were provided to the Planning Commission. This letter was in
opposition of this project due to health concerns. Ms. Pagliano shared the full paragraph from
the American Cancer Society’s website in regard to cell towers, which states “At this time, there’s
no strong evidence that exposure to RF waves from cell phone towers causes any noticeable
health effects. However, this does not mean that the RF waves from cell phone towers have been
proven to be absolutely safe. Most expert organizations agree that more research is needed to
help clarify this, especially for any possible long-term effects.” Ms. Pagliano stated that perhaps
the Empty Saddle Club sought out this lease for additional revenue. She stated that Ernie Howlett
Park could be used for the same financial benefits for the city. Ms. Pagliano stated that Verizon
should look at other locations for better coverage and stated that she is opposed to this project.

Sue Martin, 2 Empty Saddle Road, stated that she has been a resident for 27 years. She was an
active member of the Empty Saddle Club and is now an inactive member. She sat on the board
of the Empty Saddle Club and in the early 2000’s the club was looking to generate revenue
through the lease of a cell tower. It never came to fruition, likely due to regulations at the time.
Ms. Martin stated that she is opposed because she does not think it is compatible with the

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES,
OCTOBER 2, 2023
  6
 neighborhood. There is only one active member and herself, an inactive member, who are
property owners in the neighborhood. Ms. Martin stated that the Empty Saddle Club is an entity;
their concerns are different than the concerns of the residents. The South Coast Botanic Gardens
is across from her residence and stated that this should be looked into again. Ms. Martin stated

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that it would be beneficial to get clarification about

there are two required findings to obtain the additional height, which are: 1) that there are no
feasible alternate locations or designs that would allow a facility to meet the underlying zones
maximum height limit, and 2) that there are exceptional circumstances such as topography, the
existing vegetation, or structures that require a facility to meet the underlying zones maximum
height limit. She added that RHEMC Section 17.39.040(A)(3) requires co-location where possible
for new wireless facilities and new wireless facilities must affirm that no barriers to co-location for
additional personal wireless facilities will be employed. Any new wireless facilities would need to
make accommodation for co-location.

Attorney Davis stated that the issue is with RHEMC Section 17.39.040(A)(3) which states, when
feasible, facilities must consider existing and future co-locating with other personal wireless
service facilities unless it can be demonstrated that the visual effect of co-location due to
technological factors would have a greater overall negative visual impact than that of an existing
facility. This is something in the code that should be considered in regard to the additional
height.
